title_en: Why Global Bond Yields Are Surging
title_zh: 为什么全球债券收益率正在飙升｜对话 Goldman Sachs George Cole
subtitle_zh: 多重基本面叠加推动全球债市抛售、收益率升至数十年高位，低波动暗示趋势难逆。
summary_zh: 本期 Goldman Sachs Exchanges 由 Allison Nathan 对话 Goldman Sachs Research 欧洲利率策略主管 George Cole，解释为何全球债券收益率升至数十年来高位。Cole 纠正“这只是美国故事”的直觉：美国、德国、英国、日本四大政府债券市场是全球固收的核心基准，收益率都在走高，很难指认谁在引领；从 30 年期到一两年期的政策利率定价都明显更高。他认为这轮抛售有个被低估的特征：已实现波动率（realized volatility）与隐含波动率（implied volatility）在多年尺度上都相当低，因此很难归为技术性、不可持续的上行。真正的驱动是一组叠加的基本面：巨额赤字与推高政府债务的财政政策；AI 资本开支（capex）越来越多在债市融资，与政府借贷竞争；今年主要经济体增长颇具韧性；再加上伊朗战争后能源价格再度冲高的通胀冲击——高供给、私人部门发行竞争与因通胀走高而减弱的债券需求共同推高收益率。至于“为什么是现在”，近端变动更多取决于短期通胀：欧洲油价与天然气同时上涨，令英国央行（Bank of England）、欧洲央行（ECB）与美联储加息的可能性重新被定价；央行入场会推高波动，但 7 月以来长端驱动的走势更渐进有序。他也谈到以短期国库券（Treasury bills）替代长期债的债务管理操作，但收益率根本上仍由通胀与财政风险决定。给投资者的要点是：近期风险来自能源与央行是否失去耐心加息，那会令曲线前端承压、曲线变平；但在两三年到四年的尺度上，股债都与 AI 主题高度相关，五年期一段的收益率分布更不对称——若 AI capex 低于预期或去通胀更快，债券可对冲全球组合的部分敞口。
description: Why Global Bond Yields Are Surging

turns.en: Bond yields around the world have been rising for most of this year and have recently surged. So are interest rates settling into a new higher normal, or is this a temporary dislocation?
turns.zh: 今年以来，全球债券收益率已经上行了大半年，最近更是急剧飙升。那么利率到底是正在落向一个「更高的新常态」，还只是暂时的错位？

turns.en: I'm Allison Nathan and this is Goldman Sachs Exchanges. To understand why bond markets are under pressure, giving rise to higher bond yields, I'm seeing down with my colleague, George Cole, who leads European Rate Strategy for Goldman Sachs Research.
turns.zh: 我是 Allison Nathan，这里是 Goldman Sachs Exchanges。为了理解债市为何承压、债券收益率为何水涨船高，我今天和我的同事 George Cole 坐下来对谈，他负责 Goldman Sachs Research 的欧洲利率策略。

turns.en: George joins me today from London. George, welcome to the program. Thanks very much. So George, it's easy to look at the headlines and think this is just a US story.
turns.zh: George 今天从伦敦加入节目。George，欢迎上节目。非常感谢。George，我们看新闻头条，很容易觉得这只是美国的故事。

turns.en: We've obviously seen concern about inflation here in the US. There's concern about spending levels. But this bond still off is really happening everywhere.
turns.zh: 我们在美国当然看到了对通胀的担忧，也有对政府支出水平的担忧。但这轮债券抛售（sell-off）其实在全球到处都在发生。

turns.en: Is that right? Yeah. No, that's right. So as you said, I sit over here in London. I look primarily at the European bond markets in Germany and the UK.
turns.zh: 是这样吗？是的，没错。就像你说的，我坐在伦敦这边，主要看德国、英国这些欧洲国债市场。

turns.en: But when we look at the US, when we look at markets like Japan, we would really think of these four as the major government bond markets, the major benchmarks for the global economy and global fixed income markets.
turns.zh: 但当我们看美国、看日本这样的市场时，我们会把这四个市场视为主要的政府债券市场，是全球经济和全球固收市场的核心基准。

turns.en: And we're seeing all of these markets move higher in yield. We're at multi-decade highs as we read about in the financial press. We're seeing yields pressing higher across all of these economies.
turns.zh: 我们看到所有这些市场的收益率都在往上走，正如财经媒体所报道的，处于数十年来高位。我们看到各经济体的收益率都在向更高推进。

turns.en: And it doesn't look obvious that there's a single driver or a single market that is really leading the sell-off or driving it over a long period of time.
turns.zh: 而且看起来并没有一个单一的驱动因素，也没有哪一个市场或哪一样因素真正在引领或长期主导这轮抛售。

turns.en: From day to day, one move might be bigger in one of those economies. But really over the last few months, all of those markets have been pushing yields higher.
turns.zh: 按日来看，也许某个经济体的波动更大。但过去几个月里，所有这些市场都在推高收益率。

turns.en: Well, that's my follow-up to you, George, because the question is what is driving this? And my intuition would be the rest of the world is just following the US lead.
turns.zh: 这正是我想追问你的，George。问题是这背后是什么在驱动？我的直觉是世界其他地方只是在跟随美国的步调。

turns.en: But you're saying that may not be the case. Every country might be dealing with their own issues. Yeah, so as a rate strategist and as an economist, we'd be looking at yield curves and bond markets to try to think about and find clues.
turns.zh: 但你说也许并非如此，每个国家可能都在应对自己的问题。是的。作为利率策略师和经济学家，我们会从收益率曲线和债市里寻找线索，

turns.en: What is driving the move? We could look which economy might be driving it. As I said, it's not that obvious that you can point to just one of those major bond markets as driving the sell-off.
turns.zh: 去看是什么在驱动这轮波动，看哪个经济体可能在引领。正如我所说，你很难明确指出某一个主要国债市场是这轮抛售的驱动者。

turns.en: You could look at things like the shape of the yield curve. Maybe it's the front end of interest rate curves that is moving that would be associated with expectations around policy rates that might be on the move, maybe reflecting cyclical conditions, better growth, higher inflation.
turns.zh: 你可以看收益率曲线的形态。也许是曲线前端的利率在动，那与政策利率预期的变化有关，可能反映周期性状况——更好的增长、更高的通胀。

turns.en: It could be maybe the long end of the curve is moving. That could be a term-premier type of issue, the price of duration risk, maybe fiscal risks or maybe even long-term growth further out the curve.
turns.zh: 也许是曲线长端在动，那可能属于期限溢价（term premium）一类的问题，久期风险（duration risk）的定价、财政风险，甚至更远处的长期增长。

turns.en: What we're seeing across the yield curve is that all the way from the 30-year point on the curve, which has got a lot of attention and yields are much higher there than they have been in recent decades, but all the way down the 10-year point on the curve and even the policy rate expectations or pricing one or two years out is looking much higher, maybe not right at the peak of where we were in 2022, but certainly very high relative to where
turns.zh: 我们在整条收益率曲线上看到的是：从备受关注的30年期——其收益率远高于近几十年的水平——一路往下到10年期，甚至一两年期的政策利率预期或定价都明显更高。也许没有到2022年峰值的位置，但相对于近年的水平显然已经很高。

turns.en: we've been in recent years. It looks like we've got broad-based pressure across a range of different factors. What are then the fundamental drivers or are there not?
turns.zh: 我们过去几年的水平。看起来是多种不同因素在广泛施压。那么根本的驱动因素究竟是什么？还是说根本没有？

turns.en: What do you attribute all of this movement to? I'm glad you asked, are there fundamentals behind it? This is one of the features of this sell-off, I think, is a little underappreciated when you might read about it, is that actually the volatility of the moves have been relatively low.
turns.zh: 你怎么归因这一切的变动？问得好——背后有基本面吗？我认为这轮抛售有一个不太被重视的特点：这些波动的波动率其实相对较低。

turns.en: Of course, we're dealing with the revision right now of central bank expectations and we're maybe moving toward an expectation that rates will be moving higher from central banks.
turns.zh: 当然，我们眼下正在修正对央行的预期，也许正走向央行将把利率推高的预期。

turns.en: That's now inducing a little bit of volatility in the market, but if we go back to, say, July and think about the move since then in yields higher, what has been really striking is that volatility has been low, both the realized volatility of the market and also the price of volatility, the implied volatility that is priced into the market as well.
turns.zh: 这确实在市场里带来了一些波动。但如果我们回到7月左右，看那之后收益率上行的过程，真正引人注目的是波动率一直很低——无论是市场的已实现波动率（realized volatility），还是市场定价的隐含波动率（implied volatility），都很低。

turns.en: Now, we might be a little bit higher in the range of the year, but if you look at on a multi-year horizon, volatility is actually quite low.
turns.zh: 眼下波动率可能略高于年内区间的上沿，但放在多年尺度上看，波动率其实相当低。

turns.en: That feature of this sell-off makes it much harder to argue, well, this is a non-fundamental move. This is happening because of some sort of technical reason or a move in the market that has outsized volatility that is not sustainable.
turns.zh: 这轮抛售的这个特征，让你很难说这只是一个非基本面的波动，是某种技术原因导致的、或者波动过大而不可持续的上行。

turns.en: When volatility remains low, it is harder to make that conclusion. What I would say is that there is an overlapping set of fundamentals here that are driving yields up, and that goes all the way from long-running themes like large deficits, fiscal policy that is driving debt levels to historic or recent highs.
turns.zh: 当波动率保持低位，你就很难下这样的结论。我会说，是一组相互叠加的基本面在推高收益率。从长期主题开始，比如巨额赤字、把政府债务水平推到历史或近年高位的财政政策。

turns.en: We've had that since the pandemic. Now, that's not always and everywhere a guide to what markets do, but when you combine that with something that is operating over the last few years, the borrowing associated with AI capex as more and more of the AI capex is financed in debt markets, we are seeing there's some competition now for government borrowing.
turns.zh: 疫情以来一直如此。这并不总能预示市场怎么走。但当它和过去几年一直在起作用的因素叠加——与 AI 资本开支（capex）相关的借贷，因为越来越多的 AI capex 在债市融资——我们就看到政府借贷出现了竞争。

turns.en: Then the final layer, this year, we've actually had pretty resilient growth across major economies and very locally, and this is driving some of the most recent volatility, we are seeing a renewed push higher in energy prices following the ongoing war in Iran that is the last kind of inflationary push that is worrying the market.
turns.zh: 最后一层，是今年主要经济体的增长相当有韧性，而且相当有序。这正在制造一些最近的波动：我们看到在持续的伊朗战争之后，能源价格再度冲高，这是让市场担忧的最后一轮通胀冲击。

turns.en: Now, what those things are combining to do, we know we've got this backdrop of elevated government supply. We've now got competition from private sector issuance.
turns.zh: 这些因素叠加的结果是：我们已有政府债券供给高企的背景，现在又多了私人部门发行的竞争。

turns.en: Just at the moment, that bond demand is weaker because of higher inflation and actually resilient growth in the economy, and all of those things combine, we think, fundamentally to push yields up.
turns.zh: 恰好此时，因为通胀更高、经济增长有韧性，债券需求更弱。我们认为，这一切在基本面上共同推高了收益率。

turns.en: Right, but when I look at those list of factors, the most recent one, of course, has been the surge in energy prices, and so my question is why now when many of those factors have been sort of long in the market, long in coming, is that your answer is energy or it's still a question we're trying to answer?
turns.zh: 对。但当我看这些因素的清单，最新的当然是能源价格的飙升。所以我的问题是，为什么是现在——明明很多因素在市场上已经酝酿很久了？你的答案是能源吗，还是这仍是我们正在试图回答的问题？

turns.en: The move very recently, so if we think about the potential for Bank of England rate hikes or further ECB rate hikes, the potential for the Fed to hike, those things are more determined by the nearer term inflation considerations, particularly in Europe, where we've got not only rising oil prices, but also European gas prices.
turns.zh: 最近这一轮的变动——如果我们看英国央行（Bank of England）加息或欧洲央行（ECB）进一步加息的可能性、美联储加息的可能性——这些更多取决于近端通胀的考量。尤其在欧洲，我们不仅有油价上涨，还有欧洲天然气价格的上涨。

turns.en: This is creating a real headache for the inflation outlook in Europe. There's no doubt the surge from energy prices should prove temporary, but it feels like the central banks there now are running out of a bit of patience to deal with what should be temporary shocks and are willing to take a little bit more action to safeguard inflation further down the line.
turns.zh: 这给欧洲的通胀前景造成了一个真正的难题。能源价格的飙升无疑最终会被证明是暂时的，但那里的央行们似乎已不愿继续等待本该是暂时的冲击，愿意采取更多行动来守护后续的通胀。

turns.en: So you're right. That is what is driving the latest round of interest rate movements, and they have been a bit more volatile, and certainly when the central bank comes into play, that is when you do see a little bit more of a pickup in rates volatility, but that really hasn't been the story of the entire selloff.
turns.zh: 所以你说得对，这正是驱动最新一轮利率变动的东西，它们确实波动更大。当央行入场时，你确实会看到利率波动率上升。但那并不是整个抛售过程的故事。

turns.en: Not say if we rewind to something like July, the move has been more gradual, more orderly, and driven by the long end of the curve, which suggests some of these more longer running factors that you mentioned also are contributing, but I would certainly stress that it is the overlap and combination of these factors that I think gets us to where we are today.
turns.zh: 不是说如果回到7月左右——那段时间的变动更渐进、更有序，由曲线长端驱动，这说明你提到的那些更长期的因素也在起作用。但我一定要强调，正是这些因素的叠加与组合，才把我们带到今天。

turns.en: The other major development in the recent period has been that the US Treasury has been engaged in bond buybacks. Tell us more about that and its implications.
turns.zh: 近期另一个重要进展是，美国财政部（US Treasury）一直在进行债券回购（bond buybacks）。多讲讲这个以及它的影响。

turns.en: Why are they doing that? Yeah. So the bond buybacks is a program that the US Treasury have had for some years now. The idea of the program is to, if you think about the bond market, the most liquid bonds that are out there in the system are the ones that have been issued recently.
turns.zh: 他们为什么这么做？是的。债券回购是美国财政部运行多年的一个项目。设想一下债市：系统里流动性最好的债券，是最近发行的那些。

turns.en: The bonds that have been issued some time ago are less liquid, there's less turnover in these bonds, and so the buyback program is designed to take some of those less liquid bonds out of the system and replace them with fresher bonds.
turns.zh: 早些时候发行的债券流动性较差，换手率较低。所以回购项目的设计目的，就是把那些流动性差的债券移出系统，换成更新的债券。

turns.en: So if you think about that motivation, it's kind of a liquidity operation. It just greases the bond market with these newer fresher bonds. The announcement some weeks ago that we heard from the US Treasury that they would increase the size of buybacks at the long end of the curve, and the practical effect of that will be to reduce the maturity of the debt stock.
turns.zh: 从动机看，这是一种流动性操作，只是用更新的、流动性更好的债券给债市加润滑。几周前我们听到美国财政部宣布将加大曲线长端的回购规模，其实际效果是缩短债务存量的期限结构。

turns.en: You would be taking out some of these less liquid bonds, maybe over a 10 or 20 or 30 year maturity, and you would be replacing them with bonds that you're issuing usually at lower maturities and maybe even using Treasury bills.
turns.zh: 你会移除一些流动性较差、10年、20年或30年期的债券，然后用发行的较低期限债券、甚至可能是国库券（Treasury bills）来替代。

turns.en: And so in effect, this is a switch to take longer maturity but less liquid bonds out of the system and replace them with shorter maturity bonds.
turns.zh: 所以本质上，这是一种转换：把期限更长但流动性差的债券移出系统，换成期限更短的债券。

turns.en: If we think about that in the context of what other treasuries across the major economies. So the UK Debt Management Office, the DMO, is a good example of this.
turns.zh: 如果我们把这放到其他主要经济体债务管理机构的背景下看，英国债务管理办公室（DMO）就是一个好例子。

turns.en: At the end of last year, the DMO announced that they would be reducing the amount of 30 year bonds that they would be issuing to the market.
turns.zh: 去年年底，DMO 宣布将减少向市场发行的30年期债券数量。

turns.en: And that did have some effect to lower the yield in the 30 year part of the curve but only on a relative basis. Little bit of a curve effect and a little bit of an effect to support 30 year yields lower against say swap rates.
turns.zh: 那确实对压低曲线30年期收益率起到了一些作用，但只是相对意义上的。有一点曲线效应，也有一点支撑30年期收益率相对于掉期利率（swap rates）走低的效果。

turns.en: What it didn't do was change the macro price of the bond or the level of the yields. Only really the fundamentals, expectations around policy, around fiscal policy, around inflation can do that.
turns.zh: 但它并没有改变债券的宏观定价，也没有改变收益率的水平。真正能改变这些的，只有基本面，只有政策预期、财政政策预期、通胀预期。

turns.en: And again, the UK is a great example here. Despite the fact we haven't seen very many 30 year bonds issued recently, 30 year yields are still near the highs.
turns.zh: 英国同样是很好的例子。尽管最近30年期债券发得不多，30年期收益率仍在高位附近。

turns.en: And so in that sense, it's not going to change the macro fundamentals. Right, George. But I do think the market interpretation of this announcement, which I think was somewhat unexpected.
turns.zh: 所以从这个意义上说，它不会改变宏观基本面。好的，George。但我确实认为，市场对这一公告的解读——我认为这个公告多少有些出乎意料——

turns.en: Please correct me if I'm wrong, was that this wasn't an attempt by the Treasury to reduce long-end yields. But you don't think it will have that effect setting their motivations aside.
turns.zh: 如果我错了请纠正我——并不是把它视为财政部试图压低长端收益率的举动。但撇开他们的动机不谈，你也认为这不会产生那种效果，这不是你的观察吗？

turns.en: That's not your observation. Yeah. So I think that the announcement came in an unanticipated way. It was not in the regular schedule of the communication of the US Treasury to the market via its refunding announcements.
turns.zh: 是的。我认为这个公告来得出乎意料。它不在美国财政部通过再融资公告（refunding announcements）与市场沟通的常规日程里。

turns.en: And so in that sense, there was initially a bit of ambiguity about exactly what the program was designed to achieve. Part of the rationale subsequently was that there would be some attempt to improve liquidity at the long end of the curve.
turns.zh: 所以一开始，这个项目到底想实现什么有一点模糊。之后给出的部分理由是，会尝试改善曲线长端的流动性。

turns.en: And again, following the pattern that we're seeing in the other debt management offices or the other treasuries and issuers across sovereign markets, it does seem a very natural thing to try to balance the supply and demand dynamics across the yield curve.
turns.zh: 而且，遵循我们在其他债务管理机构或主权市场其他发行方看到的模式，平衡整条曲线上的供需动态确实是非常自然的选择。

turns.en: There are deficits to finance and the Treasury in the US and elsewhere need to make a decision. How do we finance that? What's the optimal way to issue that debt?
turns.zh: 赤字需要融资，美国和其他地方的财政部都需要做决定：我们如何融资？发行这些债务的最优方式是什么？

turns.en: Well, when we have a situation where yields are high, central banks are no longer buying debt. We've got reduced demand from, say, pension funds, other investors that typically buy these longer dated bonds.
turns.zh: 当我们处在收益率高企、央行不再购买国债的局面，来自养老基金等典型长债买家的需求已经减少。

turns.en: There's lower demand because at these higher yield levels, liabilities of, say, pension systems that are being discounted at these higher levels of rates, they are now much lower.
turns.zh: 需求下降的原因是：在更高的收益率水平上，用这些高利率折现的养老体系负债大幅降低了。

turns.en: And so that demand has actually fallen despite the fact yields have moved higher. And that means that treasuries and issuers, it makes a lot of sense to think about lowering the amount of longer dated issuance and relying on more liquid and shorter maturities.
turns.zh: 所以尽管收益率上行了，需求反而下降了。对财政部和发行方而言，减少长端发行、更多依赖流动性更高的短期限工具，就非常合理。

turns.en: And that's exactly what we've seen across a number of economies. So if we view that as the pattern that we're seeing across these sovereign issuers, then this increased buybacks at the long end is just a different way to do that.
turns.zh: 这正是我们在多个经济体看到的。如果把这视为这些主权发行方的共同模式，那么加大长端回购只是实现同一目标的另一种方式。

turns.en: You could reduce auction sizes or you could do these buybacks to get these longer dated bonds out of the market. In the end, the effect will be the same.
turns.zh: 你可以缩减招标规模，也可以通过回购把长债移出市场。最终效果是一样的。

turns.en: But I certainly would say the evidence across whether it's the UK, Japan, to some extent has made some steps to reduce long-end issuance, that's not really doing much to change the macro price.
turns.zh: 但我一定会说，证据表明，无论是英国、日本，还是某种程度上已采取措施减少长端发行的市场，这些做法对宏观定价的改变都很有限。

turns.en: And we are seeing yields in those markets very much being determined by the deeper fundamentals. Are there worries about inflation or fiscal risks?
turns.zh: 我们看到这些市场的收益率根本上还是由更深层的基本面决定。是否有对通胀或财政风险的担忧？

turns.en: Are there issuance pressures that are maybe outside of governments that are also leading to those higher yields? Those are the things that are really going to determine the level of yields.
turns.zh: 是否有政府之外的发行压力也在推高收益率？这些才是真正决定收益率水平的东西。

turns.en: Understood. Let's get back again to some of these drivers of these long-term bond yields reaching higher levels. We've talked about the US dealing with really an unprecedented deficit outside of war times, but there's also rising regional tensions that are forcing Europe and Asia to spend heavily on their own defense.
turns.zh: 明白。我们再回到长期债券收益率走高的那些驱动因素。我们谈到美国在非战争时期面临前所未见的赤字，但各地地缘紧张也在迫使欧洲和亚洲在国防上大力开支。

turns.en: So we are seeing sort of fiscal pressures globally. Does that really mean, again, just coming back to the drivers, that higher rates are just really simply the cost or maybe the permanent cost of today's fiscal and to some extent even geopolitical realities?
turns.zh: 所以我们看到全球性的财政压力。这是否意味着——再次回到驱动因素——更高的利率其实就是今日财政、甚至某种程度上地缘政治现实的代价，也许是永久的代价？

turns.en: Yeah. So I think that when we be looking at the fiscal outlook, what you really want to be paying attention to what are the nondiscretionary elements of the budget spending that are committed to entitlement spending, obviously a big one and has importance across all of the major economies, and interest costs.
turns.zh: 是的。我认为看财政前景时，真正要关注的是预算中的非自由裁量（nondiscretionary）部分：承诺的义务性支出（entitlement spending），这在所有主要经济体都很重要，还有利息成本。

turns.en: And this is something as we keep rolling over government debt at these higher levels of yields, this is a non-negotiable cost that governments need to pay.
turns.zh: 随着我们以更高的收益率不断滚动政府债务，这是政府必须支付的、不可协商的成本。

turns.en: So there is pressure on budgets from that source. And if you add on that commitments to increased defense spending, which as you mentioned across a number of geographies, but certainly here in Europe, that is a commitment that you're increasingly seeing governments make, the UK being a great example of that, it does lead to very challenging budget choices.
turns.zh: 所以预算在这方面有压力。如果你再加上国防开支的增长承诺——正如你所说，在很多地区、尤其在这里的欧洲，越来越多政府做出这种承诺，英国就是一个很好的例子——这会带来非常艰难的预算选择。

turns.en: You need to think how will that additional spending be financed when the budget's already under pressure? It could be via higher revenue, higher taxation.
turns.zh: 在预算已经承压的情况下，你得思考这些额外支出如何融资。可能是更高的收入、更高的税收。

turns.en: It could be via reduced spending elsewhere, or it could be by renewed borrowing. And so that's why the bond market is watching fiscal events and wants to understand exactly what priorities governments will be giving.
turns.zh: 可能是削减其他支出，也可能是重新举债。这就是为什么债市紧盯财政事件，想弄清政府会给出怎样的优先顺序。

turns.en: Of course, we're also in a situation where there is a competition for savings. And I mentioned before, we've got a situation where the private sector is undertaking a very significant uplift of capex, borrowing is being used to finance that.
turns.zh: 当然，我们也处在储蓄竞争（competition for savings）的局面。我前面提到，私人部门正在进行非常大规模的 capex 提升，借贷正被用来为此融资。

turns.en: And so just at the moment where governments are attempting this uplift in some areas of spending, there is now a competition for savings. And if we think about what that does to the savings investment balance globally, we have fewer savings, we have more investment.
turns.zh: 恰在此时，政府正试图提升某些领域的支出，于是出现了储蓄的争夺。如果我们想想这对全球储蓄-投资平衡的影响：储蓄更少，投资更多。

turns.en: And the way to clear that market is by raising interest rates. So it may not be here forever, but it certainly is an environment where at the moment while those spending pressures or spending commitments are under pressure to expand, and there's a competition for those global savings, we should expect that higher rates are part of the environment.
turns.zh: 让市场出清的方式就是抬升利率。所以也许不会永远这样，但在支出压力或支出承诺被迫扩大、全球储蓄被争夺的当下环境里，我们应该预期更高利率是环境的一部分。

turns.en: Right. Let's zoom out for a moment, George. I'm looking at the screen at over 5% tenure US yields. That seems so high to me, but if you really think about history, that was much closer to the pre-global financial crisis norm.
turns.zh: 对。我们暂时拉远视角，George。我看着屏幕上超过5%的美国国债收益率，这在我看来很高。但如果你认真看历史，这其实更接近全球金融危机前的常态。

turns.en: So in some sense, is this really just a return to a normal, potentially even healthier environment? So if you look at the long sweep of the long time series of yields, you're absolutely right.
turns.zh: 所以从某种意义上说，这是否其实只是回归一种常态、甚至可能更健康的状态？如果你看收益率的漫长历史序列，你说的完全对。

turns.en: We haven't seen these levels for many decades, maybe in some cases. But if you look at the longer history of yields, the levels that we're at are not all that unusual.
turns.zh: 我们几十年没见过这些水平了，某些市场甚至更久。但如果你看收益率的更长期历史，我们现在的位置并不算太异常。

turns.en: And I think consistent with some of the big shifts that we've seen say over the last five years or so, the most obvious one is the big shift higher in both the level and the distribution of inflation risk.
turns.zh: 我认为，与我们过去五年左右看到的一些大变化相一致，最明显的是通胀风险在水平和分布上的大幅上移。

turns.en: That if you compare that to where we were in the decade following the global financial crisis into the pandemic, couldn't be more different.
turns.zh: 把它和全球金融危机后十年直到疫情前的情形比较，再不同不过了。

turns.en: That was when we were worried about weakness in demand, very weak inflation outcomes. Policy couldn't quite generate the inflation repressure that it wanted to.
turns.zh: 那时我们担忧的是需求疲弱、通胀结果非常弱，政策几乎无法制造出它想要的通胀回升压力。

turns.en: And so the distribution of risks in the bond market was to lower yields. Now we have a distribution of inflation outcomes that looks maybe even higher than central bank targets, but certainly much more symmetric around central bank targets.
turns.zh: 所以债市的风险分布指向更低的收益率。现在我们看到的通胀结果分布，也许甚至高于央行目标，但围绕央行目标肯定对称得多。

turns.en: And in some sense, that connects us back to something that looks a little more normal relative to the decade following the global financial crisis.
turns.zh: 从某种意义上说，这让一切看起来比全球金融危机后的那十年更正常一些。

turns.en: There is one big difference, which is fiscal positions are different to where they were back in a period where yields were higher, both nominal yields and real yields.
turns.zh: 有一个很大的不同，就是财政状况与收益率更高的那个时期不同了，无论名义收益率还是实际收益率都是如此。

turns.en: We now have much bigger debt burdens. We have bigger deficits. So that is something that was much more part of the discussion. Can you have a normal yield environment this high with fiscal policy as it is currently struck?
turns.zh: 我们现在有更大的债务负担、更大的赤字。所以这正是讨论更多的部分：以当前财政政策的状态，能有这么高的正常收益环境吗？

turns.en: One of the ways I think you can delay answering that question is high nominal growth as long as growth both on the real side, but if you also have a cushion of inflation is higher, that is something that can sustain yields at these levels.
turns.zh: 我认为延后回答这个问题的一种方式就是较高的名义增长——不仅实际侧增长，如果还有通胀作为缓冲、通胀更高，那是能支撑收益率在这些水平的。

turns.en: But those are the questions for the future. How will we bear the rise in interest costs that the current yield curve would imply? And then maybe when I think about some specific markets, somewhere like Germany, the German yield curve is not yet back to levels that we saw pre-global financial crisis.
turns.zh: 但这些都是未来的问题。我们如何承受当前收益率曲线隐含的利息成本上升？然后也许当我看一些具体市场，比如德国，德国收益率曲线还没有回到全球金融危机前的水平。

turns.en: There are good reasons for that, I think, as we learned through not only the GFC, but then the European sovereign crisis, the rise of credit spreads in European sovereign markets does create a little bit of a more challenging environment to sustain much higher boon yields.
turns.zh: 我认为这有很好的理由。我们在经历全球金融危机的同时，又经历了欧洲主权债务危机，欧洲主权市场信用利差（credit spreads）的上升，确实让维持显著更高债券收益率的环境更具挑战。

turns.en: If you have high boon yields plus a credit spread to other sovereign markets in Europe, that creates much tighter financial conditions for borrowing in some of those other economies.
turns.zh: 如果你有很高的债券收益率，再加上相对于其他欧洲主权市场的信用利差，就会给那些经济体的借贷造成更紧的金融条件。

turns.en: And so there is something that is probably going to keep the distribution of German yields a little lower. On the flip side of that, we're seeing maybe now the prospect of something like sustainable 2% or something close to it in Japan in inflation.
turns.zh: 所以有些因素可能让德国收益率的分布保持在略低的位置。反过来说，我们看到日本通胀现在有望达到可持续的2%或接近2%的水平。

turns.en: And that's something we haven't seen for several decades, and so it does look like Japanese yields might be at a higher end of the range relative to what they've seen in recent decades.
turns.zh: 这是我们几十年没见过的。所以日本收益率相对于近几十年看到的区间，可能位于更高的一端。

turns.en: But if you think about the forward, George, what are you expecting in terms of rates? Will they remain at these elevated levels? Where do we go from here?
turns.zh: 但如果看向未来，George，你对利率的预期是什么？它们会维持在这些高位吗？接下来我们走向何方？

turns.en: Yeah, so going back to one of the things we mentioned before, this sell-off is broad. It's been across the curve. It's been across economies.
turns.zh: 是的。回到我们之前提到的一点，这轮抛售是广泛的，跨越整条曲线，跨越各经济体。

turns.en: And although we are maybe now witnessing something that looks a little bit more volatile as central banks come into play, generally it's been a relatively low-vol sell-off.
turns.zh: 虽然现在随着央行入场，我们看到的波动可能更大一些，但整体上是低波动的抛售。

turns.en: That tells you that there are probably fundamental views in the market behind the sell-off. So my view is it's going to take a fundamental to beat a fundamental.
turns.zh: 这告诉你市场背后可能有基本面的观点在驱动。所以我的观点是，要打败基本面，必须用另一个基本面。

turns.en: And so if you want to get yields lower, you've got to have some sort of pathway to lower inflation, I think, is the most obvious way to think about what would get yields lower.
turns.zh: 如果你想让收益率更低，就必须有某种通往更低通胀的路径。我认为这是理解什么能让收益率下行的最直观方式。

turns.en: The approximate source of that, if you wanted to think about a reversal of what's driving yields higher in the very short run, is global energy prices.
turns.zh: 如果要找一个能逆转近期推动收益率上行因素的近端来源，那就是全球能源价格。

turns.en: So both the oil market, refined products, the European gas market, that is really difficult to have a lot of conviction on in the near term, given its link to the geopolitical events, the war in Iran, and near-term visibility is really hard.
turns.zh: 无论是原油市场、成品油，还是欧洲天然气市场，鉴于其与地缘政治事件、伊朗战争的关联，短期内非常难有把握，近期可见度真的很难。

turns.en: On a six to 12-month basis, our commodity strategists do expect at some point these commodity markets are likely to be better supplied and see those prices come down.
turns.zh: 在6到12个月的尺度上，我们的大宗商品策略师确实预期，这些大宗商品市场在某个点可能会供给更充裕，看到价格回落。

turns.en: So are we still worried about energy price inflation in six to 12 months' time? We hope not. We forecast not. That would be one way to get lower yields, particularly in the front end of the curve, where central banks don't need to quite be as worried as maybe the market thinks they will be about the energy price inflation.
turns.zh: 所以6到12个月后我们还担心能源价格通胀吗？我们希望不会，我们的预测也不会。那是压低收益率的一种方式，特别是曲线前端，让央行不必像市场认为的那样担忧能源价格通胀。

turns.en: And then over the longer run, I think an interesting one is to think about what happens to this AI investment cycle. And at some point, you would imagine that investment needs will decrease once the investments begin to bear fruit.
turns.zh: 然后在更长期，一个有意思的点是想想 AI 投资周期会怎样。在某个点，你可以设想当投资开始结出果实，投资需求会下降。

turns.en: And one of the questions for the rates markets is, can you seamlessly go from the borrowing phase to the implementation phase where we transition into this world of higher growth and higher productivity?
turns.zh: 利率市场的问题之一是，你能否无缝地从借贷阶段过渡到落实阶段，进入一个更高增长、更高生产率的世界？

turns.en: That might include a higher cost of capital further down the line, but to the extent there's any bumps in that journey, if investment expectations were to fall, if there was some sort of other growth shock that could see a revision of some of those expectations, if there's maybe some of the disinflationary impacts of AI productivity growth that happen a little faster than expected, that would be the other way that you could imagine some of the pressure that we're seeing
turns.zh: 那可能意味着更后面更高的资本成本。但只要这路上有任何颠簸——如果投资预期下降，如果有某种增长冲击导致这些预期被修正，如果 AI 生产率增长带来的去通胀效应比预期来得更快一点——那就能缓解我们在债市看到的压力。

turns.en: in the bond market is alleviated. And so in that sense, those seem to me to be both in the near term and the more medium term, the most plausible drivers.
turns.zh: 从那个意义上说，这些在我看来是近期和更中期两个维度上最可能的驱动因素。

turns.en: Of course, we'd be watching things like fiscal policy very closely. And if you do see a move toward fiscal tightening or something changes in the fiscal trajectory, that would be also something as a sign for lower yields.
turns.zh: 当然，我们会非常密切关注财政政策。如果你看到向财政紧缩的转变，或者财政路径有所变化，那也会是收益率下行的一个信号。

turns.en: But as it stands, I think near term energy prices, that's what's delivering a lot of the near term movement and volatility in markets. And then the forward trajectory of the AI capex cycle is really the key thing to watch.
turns.zh: 但就现状而言，我认为近端是能源价格，那正在制造市场的近期变动和波动。然后 AI capex 周期的前进轨迹是真正要关注的核心。

turns.en: So still a lot of uncertainty, of course, around all of those factors. So what would be your key takeaway, George, for investors right now? Should they be reevaluating the duration of risk profiles within their portfolios?
turns.zh: 所以所有这些因素仍然有非常大的不确定性。那对投资者而言，你现在的关键要点是什么？他们应该重新评估组合中的久期和风险配置吗？

turns.en: Or just see how this evolves and hold tight? In the very near term, the risk to bonds is coming from the energy markets. And then I think most importantly, the connection to central bank pricing, where central banks, they just run out of road, they can't tolerate the inflation anymore and they need to hike.
turns.zh: 还是静观其变、紧抱不放？在非常近的短期，债券的风险来自能源市场。然后我认为最重要的，是与央行定价的联系——央行会不会弹尽粮绝，无法再容忍通胀，不得不加息。

turns.en: That would be the most plausible, proximate risk that would manifest in the front end. And that would be an environment where the yield curve would flatten.
turns.zh: 那会是最可能的近端风险，并会体现在曲线前端。那将是一个收益率曲线变平的环境。

turns.en: In that situation, you probably would see a decline in growth expectations, maybe inflation expectations further out the curve. That wouldn't necessarily see longer term yields a lot higher.
turns.zh: 那种情况下，你可能会看到增长预期下行，也许更远处的通胀预期也下行。那未必会让长期收益率高很多。

turns.en: You might see stability out in the forward curve. And if we think about that then, in combination with the broader investment outlook, whether it's the equity market or credit markets, a huge amount of connection to the AI investment theme, that is when you can maybe start to build a portfolio where bonds have some hedge value.
turns.zh: 你可能会看到远期曲线的稳定。如果我们将此与更广泛的投资前景——无论是股市还是信用市场，都与 AI 投资主题有巨大的联系——结合起来考虑，那时你也许可以开始构建一个债券具有某种对冲价值的组合。

turns.en: Where if we find that the AI capex trajectory undershoots expectations, or that there is some sort of disinflationary impact that comes faster than expected and rates need to move lower, that is when you can start to build a case that, although it's very uncertain what happens in the next three months, maybe yields are a little higher, certainly if we don't see any energy relief.
turns.zh: 即如果 AI capex 轨迹低于预期，或者某种去通胀效应来得比预期更快，利率需要下行，那时你就可以开始建立一种论证：尽管未来三个月会发生什么非常不确定，也许收益率会略高，特别是如果能源方面没有缓解的话。

turns.en: If you start to think about the distribution of outcomes over a two, three, four year horizon, it may start to be a little bit more asymmetric for the five year yield part of the curve, where yields can move lower and start to hedge some of the exposure that are in global investment portfolios.
turns.zh: 如果你开始思考两三年、四年期限上的结果分布，在五年期收益率这一段，也许会更不对称一些，收益率可以下行并开始对冲全球投资组合中的某些暴露。
